summary: Generates audio-rate waveforms, white noise, or pitch-controlled playback of an incoming audio/motion clip, typically at audio sample rates.
key_concepts: Audio Oscillator CHOP generates audio-rate waveforms such as sine, triangle, ramp, square, pulse, gaussian, or white noise.
Base Frequency gives cycles per second when Pitch Control is zero.
Units per Octave maps pitch-control values to octave changes, making MIDI-style pitch control possible.
A third Playback Source input can turn the operator into a pitch/time warper for audio or motion channels.
Unlike Wave CHOP or LFO CHOP, Audio Oscillator is designed for iterating audio-frequency output.

key_params.name: wavetype
key_params.note: Sine, gaussian, triangle, ramp, square, pulse, or white noise

key_params.name: frequency
key_params.note: Base cycles per second when pitch input is zero

key_params.name: offset
key_params.note: Value offset applied to generated samples

key_params.name: bias
key_params.note: Shape bias for triangle, gaussian, and square waves

key_params.name: smooth
key_params.note: Smooth pitch changes at audio-sample resolution

key_params.name: resetcondition
key_params.note: How the reset input triggers oscillator reset

key_params.name: reset
key_params.note: Hold generated channels at reset value

common_gotchas: Audio Oscillator runs at audio rates; use LFO CHOP for low-rate control signals unless audio-rate output is intentional.
Pitch-control input is logarithmic by octave, not linear Hz.
Smooth Pitch Changes costs more compute but prevents audible stepping from low-rate pitch inputs.
The third input can replace the waveform with a playback source, turning the operator into a pitch/time warper.
